correctness.rationale: The group scheme grading gives the stated semigroup in every characteristic. The four weights are units and sum to a multiple of the order, giving isolated singularities and the integral canonical height h=Σu_i. Independently computed residue ages: eight 2s at order nine and (1,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,3) at order eleven. A smooth toric refinement also justifies testing terminal/canonical discrepancies by toric divisors in arbitrary characteristic: higher exceptional discrepancies over the smooth model are positive and the relative discrepancy divisor has the indicated sign. The least interior heights are 2 and 1. The unique nonvertex junior point at order eleven forces the star fan; the star is coherent, and the quotient lattice N/Zv is Z⁴/Z(1,2,3,5), giving the stated weighted projective exceptional divisor. Rational ray matrices independently give local indices 1,2,3,5 and chart weights equivalent to the three displayed terminal types. A projective crepant resolution at order nine would be small; an ample Cartier divisor then equals the pullback of its Q-Cartier pushforward, contradicting positive degree on a contracted curve unless the morphism is an isomorphism.
residual_risks: Order-eleven uniqueness and nonexistence of a smooth crepant model are toric statements only. Order-nine nonexistence beyond the toric category is restricted to projective resolutions.

evidence: The classified empty junior tetrahedron implies terminality and no crepant ray; the minimum interior height is 2 from any nontrivial paired residue. The classified unique interior point forces its star whose normalized subvolumes are r times those barycentric coordinates. The lattice relation w_i e_i=11v−Σ_(j≠i)w_j e_j immediately reads off the weights at those indices; emptiness of the four subtetrahedra gives terminality. The no-projective-resolution upgrade follows already from terminality and Q-factoriality.

evidence: The height-one slices are clean tetrahedra; in the lattice translated by e4, use (w/r−e4, e2−e4, e3−e4) to see that the normalized volume is r and the barycentric fractional lattice is generated by w/r. Thus the volume-eleven case matches the unique T_(2,6,11) and the barycentric vector (1,2,3,5)/11 up to permutation. In the order-nine case pairs of barycentric coordinates always sum to integers since 1+8 and 2+7 equal nine; Reznick's Corollary 6 identifies emptiness exactly by this condition.

originality.rationale: The junior-simplex classification at the core is covered by the old classification of clean lattice tetrahedra: White's empty-tetrahedron theorem in the paired-weight case and the exact volume-eleven one-point tetrahedron and its barycentric weights in Reznick. The remaining asserted birational data are mechanical consequences of that exact classified geometry and standard toric rules, not a distinct theorem about Nash blowups. This is established implication, not a claim that Chen–Zuo stated the same sentences.
residual_risks: No prior publication of the literal concatenated Nash-labelled statement was established. Failure rests on an exact earlier lattice equivalence and direct implication, not on the unavailable catalogue item or an empty search.

value.rationale: The motivating examples are natural and the calculations may be useful exposition. As a research finding, however, the dichotomy re-expresses classified local lattice geometry, reads off standard chart labels, and applies the ordinary Q-factorial terminal obstruction. It establishes no additional discrepancy phenomenon or relationship to the behavior of iterated Nash blowups beyond sharing those inputs.
residual_risks: This assessment does not deny pedagogical use, or address whether extending the comparison to Nash-related birational geometry could be valuable.
